id_and_class.theory_title: Rourk’s Catecholaminergic Neuron Electron Transport Theory
id_and_class.summary: Rourk proposes that phenomenal consciousness is associated with a quantum-biological signaling mechanism in the midbrain: electron transport through ferritin and neuromelanin linking dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra and norepinephrine neurons of the locus coeruleus. This mechanism acts as a switch that helps the basal ganglia select one integrated, salient action channel from many competing ones. It is a neural-correlate theory meant to add a binding and selection mechanism to Global Neuronal Workspace accounts, not a quantum metaphysics of mind.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Selected Channel in Midbrain Electron Transport

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Phenomenal consciousness is associated with the cognitive or sensory channel that wins selection and gains energetic priority, becoming stabilized, integrated, and action-relevant.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Consciousness correlates with a specific signaling mechanism in identified neural tissue. Rourk does not claim that quantum mechanics explains subjectivity as such.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Weak emergence: experience is associated with the emergence of selected, integrated channels from ordinary neural and quantum-biological processes.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Basal-ganglia action-selection channels, dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc), norepinephrine neurons of the locus coeruleus (LC), and ferritin and neuromelanin structures capable of quantum electron transport.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through neurobiology, electrical measurement of brain tissue (such as conductive atomic-force microscopy), and links to established workspace and action-selection models.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Candidate channels formed by cortical and sensory loops through the basal ganglia; an electron-transport network among SNc and LC neurons routed through ferritin and neuromelanin; one selected channel that becomes phenomenally dominant.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (as integrated, selected, salient experience); attention; binding; action selection and volition.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Catecholaminergic neuron electron transport (CNET): a switch-like mechanism that routes energy from less active channels to more active ones, so a single channel wins without runaway competition.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Much unconscious processing forms channels first. Attention begins when a channel becomes coherent or salient enough to stand out from background signaling, and consciousness goes to the channel that gains priority.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Centered on the midbrain's substantia nigra pars compacta and locus coeruleus, working with prefrontal cortex and basal-ganglia loops.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Selection makes content action-guiding. When electron loading affects ferritin, iron release may feed calcium signaling in the SNc neurons serving the most salient channel, tying quantum electron movement to ordinary neuronal firing.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Binding means coordinating distributed cognitive and sensory signals into one selected, phenomenally dominant channel, grounded in a basal-ganglia and catecholaminergic mechanism rather than cortical synchrony or broadcast alone.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Globally broadcast contents, as described by Global Neuronal Workspace theory, are among the signals that form candidate channels in the Gurney-Prescott-Redgrave action-selection model; prefrontal cortex organizes them.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Ferritin's electron-buffering and redox properties are ancient, likely older than multicellular life, and could later have been recruited for signaling in complex nervous systems.
core_claims_and_evidence: Conductive atomic-force microscopy reportedly indicated quantum-mechanical electron transport in human substantia nigra tissue rich in ferritin and neuromelanin, but not in nearby control tissue.
Electron tunneling through ferritin particles has been experimentally observed.
Striatal dopamine release is spatially and temporally precise enough to mediate action selection.
Ferritin-rich oligodendrocyte precursor cells interconnect dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra, which Rourk reads as a possible route for the signaling CNET predicted.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Empirical neurobiology and biophysics combined with computational models of action selection.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Conductive atomic-force microscopy of substantia nigra tissue; measurements of electron tunneling in ferritin; anatomical studies of ferritin-rich cells linking dopamine neurons.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The evidence shows electron transport in tissue samples, not that this transport selects conscious contents in a living brain. As a correlate theory it identifies where selection might happen without explaining why the selected channel is experienced.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Whether ferritin and neuromelanin actually behave like quantum-dot solids in vivo, and whether CNET coordinates channel selection as proposed, remain to be shown.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Unusual among quantum theories: Rourk starts from neurobiology and invokes quantum effects only as part of a biological signaling mechanism, with no wave-function collapse or quantum computation. It fits within a physicalist, workspace-compatible picture.

AI_consciousness.rationale: The theory ties consciousness to a specific biological substrate in the midbrain and does not address whether other substrates could play the same selecting role.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since consciousness is associated with signaling in living neural tissue, nothing in the view supports its continuation after the brain dies.
